strongest_angle: Examining Arthur Conan Doyle's Sherlock Holmes and Bram Stoker's Count Dracula through academic character analyses and literary studies comparing their canonical traits, methods, and representations.

key_facts.fact: In the academic essay Doin' It In the Dark: Sherlock Holmes and Count Dracula in Fin-de-Siecle London published in 1996, author Sally Elizabeth Skinner explores Gothic literature and media analysis.
Daniel Cottom's publication Sherlock Holmes Meets Dracula explores how the meeting of Holmes and Dracula within the late nineteenth century provides a reevaluation of modern civilization.
In the literary study Detective VS Vampire - A Powerbattle, the author analyzes Loren D. Estleman's novel Sherlock Holmes vs Dracula or the Adventure of the Sanguinary Count.

According to the Dickinson College British Literature and Culture blog post by roberter, Sherlock Holmes's deductions at the beginning of the first story are compared to supernatural powers by Watson.
